# Results — Study 947 (The Buffer Ladder) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). We race **BUFR** — the laddered
wrapper that holds the Innovator S&P 500 Power Buffer ladder in one ticker — against every
do-it-yourself alternative: each single quarterly vintage (**PJAN / PAPR / PJUL / POCT**),
the **equal-weight DIY basket** of those four, the **beta-matched DIY ladder** (the basket
topped up with SPY until it carries the wrapper's equity beta), and the **beta-matched
SPY/BIL mix**. Every arm is measured **excess-of-cash** (minus BIL's total return) so the
Sharpe race is apples-to-apples. Daily **total-return** closes throughout (`yfinance`,
`auto_adjust=True`) — TR vs TR, never TR vs price. One execution lag: every estimated
weight (the basket's rebalance target, every beta) is formed on data through the close of
day `t` and applied at `t+1`. Costs are 5 bps one-way x NAV, charged on the DIY arms.
Common window 2020-08-11 → 2026-06-30 (BUFR's inception gates the race). As-of
**2026-06-30** (the partial current month is dropped).*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| BUFR, PJAN, PAPR, PJUL, POCT, SPY, BIL | 2020-08-11 → 2026-06-30 | 1,478 | Fingerprint `489cd6cd95e2` |

*Reproducibility note.* The `studies/_cache` parquet files are shared across the desk, and
BIL's was refreshed mid-build by another study's fetch. Because `auto_adjust=True` back-adjusts
the whole history when a new distribution lands, that moved the fingerprint from
`40c86fef4f60` to `489cd6cd95e2` **without moving a single figure in this document** — every
number below was re-run against the refreshed cash leg and reproduced to the last reported
decimal. This is precisely the drift the stamp exists to surface: a changed fingerprint is a
prompt to re-check, not evidence that a result moved.

Two sub-windows, reported separately and never mixed. Arms needing **no estimated weight**
(the wrapper, the four vintages, the DIY basket) race over **n = 1,477**. The
**beta-matched** arms burn the first 252 days estimating an expanding, one-day-lagged beta
and race over **n = 1,225** (2021-08-12 → 2026-06-30).

## The arms — excess-of-cash Sharpe race

| Arm | n | Ann. excess return | Vol | Excess Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **BUFR (the ladder)** | 1,477 | **+7.93%** | 10.21% | **+0.777** | +2.06 |
| PJAN | 1,477 | +6.61% | 8.62% | +0.767 | +2.08 |
| PAPR | 1,477 | +5.32% | 7.75% | +0.687 | +1.82 |
| PJUL | 1,477 | +7.21% | 8.20% | +0.879 | +2.40 |
| POCT | 1,477 | +7.33% | 7.77% | **+0.943** | +2.65 |
| **DIY basket (equal-weight, quarterly)** | 1,477 | +6.61% | 7.74% | **+0.853** | +2.30 |
| Beta-matched DIY ladder | 1,225 | +7.34% | 11.12% | +0.661 | +1.59 |
| Beta-matched SPY/BIL mix (to BUFR's beta) | 1,225 | +6.09% | 9.80% | +0.621 | +1.50 |
| Beta-matched SPY/BIL mix (to the basket's beta) | 1,225 | +4.59% | 6.87% | +0.668 | +1.62 |
| SPY (the underlying) | 1,477 | +13.73% | 16.92% | +0.812 | +2.17 |

**The wrapper earns more and is worth less.** BUFR's +7.93%/yr beats the DIY basket's
+6.61%/yr, but it does so with 10.21% vol against the basket's 7.74% — so its excess Sharpe
(**+0.777**) is *below* the basket's (**+0.853**) and below two of the four single vintages
it wraps. Bought one at a time, POCT alone returned a **+0.943** Sharpe.

## Absolute (lived) max drawdown, nominal total return

| BUFR | DIY basket | PJAN | PAPR | PJUL | POCT | SPY |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **−13.73%** | **−10.82%** | −11.93% | −11.87% | −10.69% | −10.22% | −24.50% |

The wrapper's worst loss is **~3 pp deeper** than the home-made basket's and deeper than
every one of its own constituents. Laddering did not buy a smoother ride here; it bought a
bumpier one, for the same reason it earned more — it carries more beta.

## The gaps — wrapper minus each DIY alternative

| Comparison | n | Gap (pp/yr) | HAC *t* | Tracking error | ΔSharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| vs **DIY basket** | 1,477 | **+1.33** | **+1.18** | 3.52% | **−0.076** |
| vs PJAN | 1,477 | +1.32 | +1.26 | 3.78% | +0.010 |
| vs PAPR | 1,477 | +2.61 | +1.74 | 4.70% | +0.090 |
| vs PJUL | 1,477 | +0.73 | +0.55 | 4.01% | −0.102 |
| vs POCT | 1,477 | +0.61 | +0.40 | 4.37% | −0.166 |
| vs **beta-matched DIY ladder** | 1,225 | **−0.96** | **−1.69** | 2.35% | −0.057 |
| vs beta-matched SPY/BIL mix | 1,225 | +0.30 | +0.31 | 2.66% | −0.018 |
| *DIY basket* vs beta-matched SPY/BIL mix | 1,225 | +1.26 | +1.39 | 2.29% | +0.043 |

**No gap in this table clears |*t*| = 2 — in either direction.** The wrapper's apparent
+1.33 pp/yr edge over the DIY basket dissolves the moment beta is held constant: BUFR's
SPY-beta is **0.579** against the four-vintage basket's **0.439** (expanding, one-day-lagged;
identical to the full-sample in-sample estimate). Add SPY to the DIY basket until it carries
the wrapper's beta, and the wrapper **loses by −0.96 pp/yr**. The two arms are 0.960
correlated day to day.

## Block bootstrap (2,000 draws, 21-day blocks, paired resampling)

| Quantity | Point | 95% CI | share < 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Gap vs DIY basket | +1.33 pp/yr | [−0.81, +3.22] | 10.2% |
| Gap vs beta-matched DIY ladder | −0.96 pp/yr | **[−1.91, −0.05]** | 98.4% |
| Sharpe gap vs DIY basket | −0.076 | [−0.209, +0.034] | 91.2% |

The un-matched gap straddles zero comfortably. The beta-matched gap's bootstrap CI *just*
clears zero at the 95% level while its HAC *t* is only −1.69 — so we audited the one CI in
this study that excludes zero.

### Does that exclusion survive the block length? No.

The block length is a free parameter of the bootstrap, not a property of the tape. Sweeping
it (three RNG seeds per setting, 2,000 draws each) on the beta-matched gap:

| Block | Mean 95% CI | Excludes zero |
|---|--:|--:|
| 5 days | [−2.20, +0.26] | 0 / 3 seeds |
| 10 days | [−2.00, +0.06] | 0 / 3 seeds |
| **21 days** (our headline) | [−1.87, −0.06] | 3 / 3 seeds |
| 42 days | [−1.81, −0.13] | 3 / 3 seeds |
| 63 days | [−1.78, −0.14] | 3 / 3 seeds |

**The exclusion is an artefact of the block length: 9 of 15 (block, seed) settings exclude
zero, 6 do not.** Flip to a 5- or 10-day block and the same gap straddles zero. A finding
that changes verdict when you change a nuisance parameter is not a finding; the HAC *t* of
**−1.69**, which prices the autocorrelation directly instead of resampling around it, is the
honest summary, and it is the one this study is stamped on. (The contrast is instructive:
on the synthetic panel with a genuinely planted premium, the CI excludes zero at *every*
block length — that is what a real gap looks like under this same sweep, and it is asserted
in the test-suite.) Verdict on this line: **suggestive of a small fee drag, short of the
desk's |*t*| ≥ 2 bar, and not rescued by the bootstrap.**

## The thing laddering is supposed to fix — how big is entry-point luck?

| Measure | Value |
|---|--:|
| Rolling 1-year best-minus-worst vintage spread — mean / median / max | 4.53 / 4.51 / 8.70 pp |
| SD of rolling 1-year returns, single vintages (PJAN/PAPR/PJUL/POCT) | 7.55 / 6.37 / 6.80 / 6.38% |
| SD of rolling 1-year returns, equal-weight basket | 6.61% |
| **Variance reduction from averaging four vintages — 1-year holding period** | **2.4%** |
| **Variance reduction from averaging four vintages — daily returns** | **4.2%** |
| Closed form at ρ = 0.889, N = 4: √((1 + 3ρ)/4) | **4.2%** |
| Mean pairwise daily correlation between vintages | **0.889** |

This is the study's real finding, and it needs no *t*-test. The four vintages are **0.889
correlated day to day**, so equal-weighting them removes almost nothing. The textbook result
for N equally-correlated legs — sd(basket)/sd(leg) = √((1 + (N−1)ρ)/N) — predicts a **4.2%**
reduction in daily standard deviation at ρ = 0.889 and N = 4; the tape delivers **4.20%**.
On a one-year *holding period*, where each vintage's path effects matter, the reduction is
smaller still at **2.4%** (6.77% → 6.61%). Entry-point luck is worth about 4.5 pp of
dispersion between the luckiest and unluckiest vintage in a given year, and averaging it away
buys you roughly a sixth of a percentage point of annual-return standard deviation.
Laddering is a real but very small piece of diversification, and it is *free* — anyone can
do it with four trades.

## Robustness

### Era cut (split 2023-07-01)

| Era | n | exSharpe wrapper / DIY | vs DIY basket | vs beta-matched DIY |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2020-08 → 2023-06 | 726 | +0.639 / +0.768 | +1.08 pp (*t* = +0.54) | **−1.22 pp** (*t* = −1.18) |
| 2023-07 → 2026-06 | 751 | +0.961 / +0.945 | +1.57 pp (*t* = +1.36) | **−0.79 pp** (*t* = −1.14) |

The beta-matched shortfall is negative in **both** halves and never significant in either.
Nothing flips sign; nothing crosses the bar.

### Cost sweep (one-way bps, charged on the DIY arms only)

| Cost | vs DIY basket | vs beta-matched DIY |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +1.32 pp (*t* = +1.18) | −0.96 pp (*t* = −1.69) |
| 5 bps | +1.33 pp (*t* = +1.18) | −0.96 pp (*t* = −1.69) |
| 25 bps | +1.33 pp (*t* = +1.19) | −0.95 pp (*t* = −1.66) |

Friction is irrelevant here, and the direction is worth stating: costs fall on the *home-made*
arms, so a higher cost can only *flatter* the wrapper. Even at a punitive 25 bps one-way
the wrapper still fails to beat a beta-matched DIY ladder. Rebalancing the DIY basket never,
annually, quarterly or monthly moves its Sharpe by less than 0.001 (+0.853 in all four
cases) — four highly-correlated legs barely drift apart.

### Assumed extra-fee sweep — a declared PROXY, not a tape measurement

A single Power Buffer vintage quotes a **0.79%/yr** expense ratio; the laddered wrapper adds
a management fee on top of those acquired-fund fees, an incremental layer we take as
**0.20%/yr** (ASSUMPTION — the exact number depends on how the acquired-fund fee waiver is
counted, so we sweep it). Published NAV total returns are already net of whatever was
charged; this sweep adds the layer back to ask "would the ladder have won if the extra layer
were waived?".

| Extra layer waived | vs DIY basket | vs beta-matched DIY |
|---|--:|--:|
| +0.00%/yr | +1.33 pp (*t* = +1.18) | −0.96 pp (*t* = −1.69) |
| +0.20%/yr (our assumption) | +1.53 pp (*t* = +1.36) | −0.76 pp (*t* = −1.34) |
| +0.40%/yr (a generous upper bound) | +1.73 pp (*t* = +1.54) | −0.56 pp (*t* = −0.98) |

The assumed fee explains roughly **a fifth to a half** of the beta-matched shortfall, and no
plausible value of it turns the wrapper into a winner. The verdict does not rest on the
guess.

### Calendar-year total return (%, complete years only)

| Year | BUFR | PJAN | PAPR | PJUL | POCT | DIY basket | Vintage spread | SPY |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2021 | +11.88 | +8.80 | +7.51 | +7.20 | +9.45 | +8.25 | 2.26 pp | +28.73 |
| 2022 | **−7.57** | −5.29 | −4.29 | −2.08 | −1.25 | **−3.20** | 4.04 pp | −18.18 |
| 2023 | +19.63 | +18.18 | +16.45 | +19.87 | +20.12 | +18.66 | 3.67 pp | +26.18 |
| 2024 | +14.68 | +13.45 | +12.28 | +13.76 | +9.55 | +12.26 | 4.21 pp | +24.89 |
| 2025 | +12.44 | +11.29 | +6.58 | +12.78 | +10.99 | +10.40 | 6.19 pp | +17.72 |

BUFR out-returned the DIY basket in every complete year — and lost more than double in
**2022**, the one year the buffers were called on. That single line is the beta story in
miniature: in the only genuine down-year of the sample, the wrapper you bought *for* downside
protection protected you less than four of its own vintages held equally.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof — never supports the stamp)

| Panel | Planted gap | Recovered | Error | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Planted laddering premium (4%/yr, less a 0.20%/yr fee) | +3.80 pp/yr | **+4.16** | +0.36 | **+4.84** |
| Null with fee only | −0.20 pp/yr | +0.16 | +0.36 | +0.18 |
| Clean null (no premium, no fee) | 0.00 pp/yr | +0.36 | +0.36 | +0.42 |

Across **8 null seeds**: mean gap +0.11 pp/yr (sd 0.87), max |*t*| = 1.69, fires (|*t*| ≥ 2)
on **0/8**. The detector recovers a genuine laddering premium at *t* ≈ 4.8 and stays quiet
when there is none — so the real-tape null is a fact about the tape, not a broken harness.

## Verdict

- **Signal — None.** The claim that laddering adds something a private investor cannot
  replicate does not survive contact with the tape. **No gap clears |*t*| = 2 in either
  direction**: +1.33 pp/yr vs the DIY basket (*t* = +1.18, bootstrap CI [−0.81, +3.22]) and
  −0.96 pp/yr vs a beta-matched DIY ladder (*t* = −1.69; its bootstrap CI excludes zero at a
  21-day block and straddles it at 5 and 10 days, so the exclusion is the block length
  talking, not the tape). The wrapper's headline outperformance
  is **beta, not laddering** — SPY-beta 0.579 vs the basket's 0.439 — and on risk-adjusted
  terms the wrapper is *worse*: excess Sharpe +0.777 vs the basket's +0.853 and POCT's +0.943,
  with a 3 pp deeper drawdown. Meanwhile the entry-point luck laddering exists to average away
  is nearly nothing: the vintages are 0.889 correlated and the basket cuts one-year return
  variance by **2.4%**. **Survivorship:** BUFR and these four vintages are the *surviving*
  flagships of a category that has launched and shuttered products; the panel flatters the
  funds, and there is exactly **one** laddered wrapper with this history — an n-of-1 product
  test, not a cross-section. **Sample:** 5.9 years, one genuine down-year (2022).
- **Tradability — Mirage.** There is nothing to bank. Buying the wrapper for laddering pays
  an extra fee layer (~0.20 pp/yr assumed, swept) for a diversification benefit measured at
  2.4% of variance and a beta tilt you could buy with an S&P 500 ETF. Trading the other way —
  shorting the wrapper against a beta-matched DIY ladder — targets a −0.96 pp/yr edge across a
  2.35% tracking error at *t* = −1.69, which is not a trade, it is a coin-flip with a
  borrow bill. Both arms also merely **tie** the dumb beta-matched SPY/BIL mix
  (+0.30 pp/yr, *t* = +0.31), reproducing Study 624's result one layer up the wrapper stack.
- **What the ladder *is* good for.** One trade instead of four, no rebalance calendar, no
  vintage to choose. That convenience is real and this study does not price it — but it is
  convenience, and it is not an edge.
